key_insight: Using Evolutionary Strategies (ES) as a gradient-free way to continue-training LLMs induces severe catastrophic forgetting — ES can rapidly overwrite previously learned behaviors despite being memory-efficient.
problem_solved: Examines whether ES can be a practical, low-memory alternative for continual learning in deployed LLMs and uncovers its suitability (or lack thereof) for preserving past knowledge.
method: Empirically evaluate ES-based continual fine-tuning on LLM benchmarks/tasks and measure retained vs. lost capabilities over time.
Compare forgetting and performance trajectories between ES and standard gradient-based continual learning baselines.
Analyze failure modes (e.g., parameter drift, distributional shift) to identify why ES induces catastrophic forgetting.
impact: Alerts practitioners that although ES reduces memory requirements, it can compromise model stability and long-term retention — prompting caution and motivating development of hybrid or mitigative continual-learning strategies.
visual_elements: Line chart: task performance over time showing rapid decline (forgetting) for ES vs. stable or slower decline for gradient-based methods.
Bar chart: final retained accuracy or knowledge retention comparing ES and gradient-based baselines across tasks.
Diagram: schematic comparing memory footprint and update mechanism of ES vs. gradient methods (icons for gradients vs. population samples).
Heatmap or parameter-change visualization: showing which parameters shift most under ES and correlate with performance loss.
paper_title: Evolutionary Strategies lead to Catastrophic Forgetting in LLMs
paper_authors: Immanuel Abdi, Akshat Gupta, Micah Mok, Alexander Lu, Nicholas Lee
